messages.body_plain:
Hi.

[I reply to the list because part of my reply is useful to others as well]

On Wed, Feb 20, 2008 at 2:06 PM, Elizabeth Purdom
<epu...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> Hi Henrik,
>
>  Okay, so I don't think I understand the concept of static function, but
>  that's a different issue.

I borrow the concept of a "static method" from Java.  It is a method
that "belongs" to a class and that you can call without having an
instance of that class.  For instance, when we load a CEL set we do
not have an instance of AffymetrixCelSet available but we want to load
one, i.e.

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName(...)

The alternative would be do do:

dummy <- AffymetrixCelSet()
cs <- byName(dummy, ...)

A more commonly seen solution in R for the above is to come up with a
long function name like:

cs <- setupAffymetrixCelSetByName(...)

but the it takes a human to infer that it actually returns an
AffymetrixCelSet, which is why we use static (class) method instead.

Another, more basic example, is when you use:

library(R.oo)
obj <- Object()
obj$foo <- 2
save(obj, file="foo.Rbin")

and later want to load that same Object:

library(R.oo)
obj <- Object$load("foo.Rbin")

>
>  Regardless, I'm wondering is it bad to have .list method that doesn't
>  assume that the list is a list of AffymetrixCelFile objects?
>  plotDensity.list appears to assume this (my most recent post about
>  this). But I think I need to take this offline, because this is perhaps
>  just a developer's question. Repost it if you think best. And ignore
>  this if I'm understanding the subsetting of the AffymetrixCelSet
>  incorrectly -- or read my post first...

The problem is that the implementation in 'aroma.light' (just like
'limma', 'affy' etc) cannot know about 'aroma.affymetrix'.  There are
plotDensity() implementation in 'aroma.light' for matrices and lists.
The 'list' implementation allows you to plot the density for numeric
vectors of different lengths.  That the plotDensity() in
aroma.affymetrix has the same name is "just a coincidence".

Details: There is no way to setup an S3 method (neither a S4 method)
to "test" also for the class of each element of the list.  That is
instead taken care of by the generic error detection in R, hence you
"strange" error message.  It is still caught as an error though.

So, unfortunately, it is not easy to have a generic plotDensity()
function that operates on a list of either numeric vectors or other
data types/classes.

>
>  Here's what I mean. I have made a function plotBoxplot with methods
>  .QualityAssessment, .AffymetrixCelSet
>  and .AffymetrixCelFile. I also have a function plotBoxplot.list which is
>  used by these functions and roughly takes as the input a list of the
>  output of boxplot.stats -- a list of things not related to any
>  aroma.affymetrix object but just generally because of the akward nature
>  of the required input to bxp. So it's a 'helper' function, but also
>  something that allows the replotting of the output of these functions
>  without doing the calculation. Example:
>  out<-plotBoxplot(qam)
>  calls the calculation function as well as plotBoxplot.list; out is a
>  list of the output of the boxplot stats. Then
>  plotBoxplot(out)
>  will seamlessly replot it. So that's good, I think. And it's an awfully
>  useful function in general, I must say, because I'm frequently wanting this.

So, ideally grDevices::boxplot.stats() would not just return a 'list'
but a list with class attribute c("BoxplotStats", "list").  Then you
could write the following to better control for the class:

setMethodS3("plotBoxplot", "BoxplotStats", function(obj, ...) {
  < the current implementation you have >
})

>
>  But shouldn't plotBoxplot.list take as input a list of AffymetrixCelFile
>  and basically call plotBoxplot.AffymetrixCelFile on each of the entries,
>  like plotDensity. Or is that just special to plotDensity? (you mentioned
>  you wanted to get rid of any need for the arrays=... option)
>  Logically, I should be able to call for an AffymetrixCelSet
>  out<-plotBoxplot(cs[1:5])
>  but this wouldn't work in how I have it now.
>
>  My solution (unimplemented) is for plotBoxplot.list to check what kind
>  of objects are in the list. Is this how I should do it?

See my explanation of plotDensity() for lists above and the trade-off
of choosing what it should do.

The easiest way to subset of arrays and still get what you want is:

  out <- plotBoxplot(extract(cs, 1:5))

Details: extract(cs, 1:5) returns another AffymetrixCelSet with only
arrays 1 to 5.  However, as we discussed offline, this will calculate
the summary only based on this subset.

The idea is to write a method for AffymetrixCelSet (or a subclass of
it) when you want to do something on a set of CEL files.  Do not work
with a 'list' of CEL files (that is what the AffymetrixCelSet class is
for in the first place).

Please do not use '[' operators on AffymetrixCelSet objects etc,
because it is still not decided how they should work/be defined.  [I
guess I should basically turn the off].

Ok, there are a lot of generic as well as specific details here, but I
hope I at least managed to guide in the right direction.  If not, let
me know.

Henrik

>
>  Best,
>  Elizabeth

>
>
>
>  Henrik Bengtsson wrote:
>  > On Wed, Feb 20, 2008 at 10:45 AM, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>  >
>  >>  Hi,
>  >>
>  >>  I have one function for the boxplot stuff that isn't for a particular
>  >>  class and I don't really understand how to use setMethodS3 for it. I
>  >>  could just make it a method for 'list' since the input needs to be that,
>  >>  but it's not going to be a function with lots of methods for different
>  >>  classes. So I think it needs to be a 'static' command, but I don't
>  >>  understand how to set it up.
>  >>
>  >
>  > So, I guess you just suggested
>  >
>  > setMethodS3("convertBoxplotStats", "list", function(boxplotStats, ...) {
>  >    ...
>  > })
>  >
>  > yourself, which I think is slightly better than:
>  >
>  >
>  >>  Currently I have the standard function definition,
>  >>
>  >>  convertBoxplotStats<-function(boxplotStats){
>  >>      ...
>  >>  }
>  >>
>  >>  How would this convert over in setMethodS3?
>  >>
>  >
>  > I'm not sure about that turning it into a static method of a class
>  > will make it better?!?  What class would you then want to couple the
>  > method to?
>  >
>  > I'm not sure what the real problem is.
>  >
>  > /Henrik
>  >
>  >
>  >
>  >>  (Maybe this is really a question for another list regarding the other
>  >>  packages that aroma.affymetrix uses?)
>  >>

On Feb 21, 2008, at 2:42 PM, Henrik Bengtsson wrote:

>
> Hi.

> [I reply to the list because part of my reply is useful to others as
> well]
>
> On Wed, Feb 20, 2008 at 2:06 PM, Elizabeth Purdom
> <epu...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
>> Hi Henrik,
>>
>> Okay, so I don't think I understand the concept of static function,
>> but
>> that's a different issue.
>
> I borrow the concept of a "static method" from Java.  It is a method
> that "belongs" to a class and that you can call without having an
> instance of that class.  For instance, when we load a CEL set we do
> not have an instance of AffymetrixCelSet available but we want to load
> one, i.e.
>
> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName(...)
>
> The alternative would be do do:
>
> dummy <- AffymetrixCelSet()
> cs <- byName(dummy, ...)
>
> A more commonly seen solution in R for the above is to come up with a
> long function name like:
>
> cs <- setupAffymetrixCelSetByName(...)
>
> but the it takes a human to infer that it actually returns an
> AffymetrixCelSet, which is why we use static (class) method instead.
>
> Another, more basic example, is when you use:
>
> library(R.oo)
> obj <- Object()
> obj$foo <- 2
> save(obj, file="foo.Rbin")
>
> and later want to load that same Object:
>
> library(R.oo)
> obj <- Object$load("foo.Rbin")
>
>>
>> Regardless, I'm wondering is it bad to have .list method that doesn't
>> assume that the list is a list of AffymetrixCelFile objects?
>> plotDensity.list appears to assume this (my most recent post about
>> this). But I think I need to take this offline, because this is
>> perhaps
>> just a developer's question. Repost it if you think best. And ignore
>> this if I'm understanding the subsetting of the AffymetrixCelSet
>> incorrectly -- or read my post first...
>
> The problem is that the implementation in 'aroma.light' (just like
> 'limma', 'affy' etc) cannot know about 'aroma.affymetrix'.  There are
> plotDensity() implementation in 'aroma.light' for matrices and lists.
> The 'list' implementation allows you to plot the density for numeric
> vectors of different lengths.  That the plotDensity() in
> aroma.affymetrix has the same name is "just a coincidence".
>
> Details: There is no way to setup an S3 method (neither a S4 method)
> to "test" also for the class of each element of the list.  That is
> instead taken care of by the generic error detection in R, hence you
> "strange" error message.  It is still caught as an error though.
>
> So, unfortunately, it is not easy to have a generic plotDensity()
> function that operates on a list of either numeric vectors or other
> data types/classes.
>
>>
>> Here's what I mean. I have made a function plotBoxplot with methods
>> .QualityAssessment, .AffymetrixCelSet
>> and .AffymetrixCelFile. I also have a function plotBoxplot.list
>> which is
>> used by these functions and roughly takes as the input a list of the
>> output of boxplot.stats -- a list of things not related to any
>> aroma.affymetrix object but just generally because of the akward
>> nature
>> of the required input to bxp. So it's a 'helper' function, but also
>> something that allows the replotting of the output of these functions
>> without doing the calculation. Example:
>> out<-plotBoxplot(qam)
>> calls the calculation function as well as plotBoxplot.list; out is a
>> list of the output of the boxplot stats. Then
>> plotBoxplot(out)
>> will seamlessly replot it. So that's good, I think. And it's an
>> awfully
>> useful function in general, I must say, because I'm frequently
>> wanting this.
>
> So, ideally grDevices::boxplot.stats() would not just return a 'list'
> but a list with class attribute c("BoxplotStats", "list").  Then you
> could write the following to better control for the class:
>
> setMethodS3("plotBoxplot", "BoxplotStats", function(obj, ...) {
>  < the current implementation you have >
> })
>
>>
>> But shouldn't plotBoxplot.list take as input a list of
>> AffymetrixCelFile
>> and basically call plotBoxplot.AffymetrixCelFile on each of the
>> entries,
>> like plotDensity. Or is that just special to plotDensity? (you
>> mentioned
>> you wanted to get rid of any need for the arrays=... option)
>> Logically, I should be able to call for an AffymetrixCelSet
>> out<-plotBoxplot(cs[1:5])
>> but this wouldn't work in how I have it now.
>>
>> My solution (unimplemented) is for plotBoxplot.list to check what
>> kind
>> of objects are in the list. Is this how I should do it?
>
> See my explanation of plotDensity() for lists above and the trade-off
> of choosing what it should do.
>
> The easiest way to subset of arrays and still get what you want is:
>
>  out <- plotBoxplot(extract(cs, 1:5))
>
> Details: extract(cs, 1:5) returns another AffymetrixCelSet with only
> arrays 1 to 5.  However, as we discussed offline, this will calculate
> the summary only based on this subset.
>
> The idea is to write a method for AffymetrixCelSet (or a subclass of
> it) when you want to do something on a set of CEL files.  Do not work
> with a 'list' of CEL files (that is what the AffymetrixCelSet class is
> for in the first place).
>
> Please do not use '[' operators on AffymetrixCelSet objects etc,
> because it is still not decided how they should work/be defined.  [I
> guess I should basically turn the off].
>
> Ok, there are a lot of generic as well as specific details here, but I
> hope I at least managed to guide in the right direction.  If not, let
> me know.
>
> Henrik
>
>>
>> Best,
>> Elizabeth
>>
>>
>>

versions are dated 2008-02-14 (Feb 14, 2008) or newer.  If you don't

today, you will not even notice the transition.

and I'll show you how to make them compatible with the upcoming
package version.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Mon, Feb 25, 2008 at 12:01 PM, JP <playb...@yahoo.com> wrote:
>
>   I understand that your program can import APT total CN estimates.  I
>   wonder if a reverse action can be done. That is if you can output the
>   total CN values to an output text files after low-level processing
>   (Fragment length adjustment).  That would allow one to generate UGP
>   file in correct order and also allow one to use the total CN
>  elsewhere.

The order of the rows in a UGP table/file is uniquely specified by the
order of the units in the corresponding CDF.  There is one UGP file
per CDF.  Please see below comments on how to create a UGP file (from
my reply in thread 'can I analyze custom array?', 2008-02-21):

<quote> ("with some minor corrections")
> You will need to setup a so called Unit Genome Position (UGP)
> annotation file which contains  a (unit, chromosome, position) map
> specific to given CDF.  If you have a NetAffx containing this
> information, you can follow the instructions on how it was done for
> the GenomeWideSNP_6,Full.cdf:
>
>  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/genomewidesnp-6---miscellaneous
>
> If you don't have a NetAffx-like data file, you can still allocate an
> empty UGP file, e.g.
>
> ugp <- AromaUgpFile$allocateFromCdf(cdf, tags="JP20080221");
> print(ugp)
>
> and populate the UGP map yourself, e.g.
>
> #  Set the chromosomes for the first seven units
> ugp[1:7,1] <- c(1,1,2,2,3,4,5)
>
> #  ...and their physical positions
> ugp[1:7,2] <- c(13410,43031,10322,10323,34303,12304,40335)
>
> Note that the rows in the UGP table should map one-to-one to the units
> in the CDF, e.g.
>
> unitName <- "SNP_A-123231"
> unit <- indexOf(cdf, unitName)
> stopifnot(getUnitNames(cdf, unit), unitName)
>
> ...and the genome position for this unit should be:
>
> print(ugp[unit,])
</quote>

When you understand how to create an UGP as above, you'll see that it
does not make sense to  go via an APT file.  An Affymetrix APT file
contains CN estimates but an UGP file in independent of measurement
data as it only contains annotation data.  They are non-related
concepts. I also don't think that Affymetrix have specified a rule how
to order the units in an APT file (though it is likely that it use the
same order as the CDF).

Hope this explains how you create an UGP file and how to populate it
with data for your chip type.

Cheers

/Henrik

Thank you for your help, I really appreciate it.  Since the Linus version seems to work, it is not a big problem for me now.

  Thanks again,

 Yue

On 2/25/08, Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I've been trying to figure what is going wrong, but I cannot reproduce
> it.  The files you've sent me show that there is nothing strange with
> the data being fitted.  My best guess is that the external algorithm
> is launched but somehow it chokes and gives up resulting in an "empty"
> output.  The only way forward I can see is to narrow down the problem
> using the actually machine that cause the problem.  If someone else
> gets/can reproduce the same problem that will give lead to go forward.
>
> So, unfortunately there is nothing more I can from my side, and I have
> to leave this as a open problem/bug (of the 'sfit' package).
>
> /Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

Please let us know what print(csRawList) outputs.  Basically, I guess
your CEL files are named something like:

rawData/
  Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal/
    Mapping250K_Nsp/
      CRL-2325D_Nsp.CEL
      ...
    Mapping250K_Sty/
      CRL-2325D_Sty.CEL
      ...

You have to rename the CEL files by replacing 'all _' (underscores)
with ',' (commas) to have filenames like CRL-2325D,Nsp.CEL and
CRL-2325D,Sty.CEL.  The *name* of a CEL file is defined in
aroma.affymetrix as the part of the filename before the first comma
(if any), i.e. with commas both CEL files have name 'CRL-2325D'.  All
other parts (except the filename extension) are referred to as *tags*,
i.e. the two CEL files have tags 'Nsp' and 'Sty', respectively.   If
you don't replace the underscores with commas, the name pf the two
files are 'CRL-2325D_Nsp' and 'CRL-2325D_Sty' and aroma.affymetrix
will not recognize them as being paired.  For more information on this
filename/directory name "grammar", please see Page 'Names, tags, and
filenames' at:

  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/file--pathnames-2

In other words, there is most likely no bug.  I have updated the
Vignette 'Paired total copy number analysis' explaining this.

You do not have to reran the analysis if you rename the CEL files
under rawData/.  Just rename the corresponding CEL files under
probeData/ and plmData/ as well.  Most likely you should delete the
files under the cbsData/Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal/ directory.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] UGP and UFL files?
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] UGP and UFL files?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

short answer: I have not made an explicit comparison, but most likely
it will not make any difference to your biological findings.

Long answer: I don't know the *exact* details on how dChip annotation
files (SNP information file and genome information file) were
generated.  However, from http://www.dchip.org/ one can read that the
source  for its files are the Affymetrix NetAffx CSV files (aka
"annotation CSV files").  These are also the ones used to create the
UGP and UFL files (all details on the aroma.affymetrix web site).

So, with everything else the same, it comes down to what version of
NetAffx was used.  From now on the UGP and UFL files will have a tag
specifying what version of NetAffx was used and also a tag indicating
who and when that person created the file, e.g.
'Mapping250K_Nsp,na24,HB20080214.ugp' will tell you that NetAffx
release/version 24 (tag 'na24') and that user 'HB' (me) created the
file on 2008-02-14.  dChip "tags" the annotation files with the genome
build instead, e.g. 'hg18'.  In other words, it is a bit ambiguous
what NetAffx version dChip use, but my best guess is that Cheng Li
updates the annotation files quarterly when NetAffx get updated.

In summary, my best guess is that any differences are only minor and
won't affect your results significantly.

/Henrik

> Hi.
>
> Please let us know what print(csRawList) outputs.  Basically, I guess
> your CEL files are named something like:
>
> rawData/
> Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal/
>    Mapping250K_Nsp/
>      CRL-2325D_Nsp.CEL
>      ...
>    Mapping250K_Sty/
>      CRL-2325D_Sty.CEL
>      ...
>
> You have to rename the CEL files by replacing 'all _' (underscores)
> with ',' (commas) to have filenames like CRL-2325D,Nsp.CEL and
> CRL-2325D,Sty.CEL.  The *name* of a CEL file is defined in
> aroma.affymetrix as the part of the filename before the first comma
> (if any), i.e. with commas both CEL files have name 'CRL-2325D'.  All
> other parts (except the filename extension) are referred to as *tags*,
> i.e. the two CEL files have tags 'Nsp' and 'Sty', respectively.   If
> you don't replace the underscores with commas, the name pf the two
> files are 'CRL-2325D_Nsp' and 'CRL-2325D_Sty' and aroma.affymetrix
> will not recognize them as being paired.  For more information on this
> filename/directory name "grammar", please see Page 'Names, tags, and
> filenames' at:
>
> http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/file--pathnames-2
>
> In other words, there is most likely no bug.  I have updated the
> Vignette 'Paired total copy number analysis' explaining this.
>
> You do not have to reran the analysis if you rename the CEL files
> under rawData/.  Just rename the corresponding CEL files under
> probeData/ and plmData/ as well.  Most likely you should delete the
> files under the cbsData/Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal/ directory.
>
> Hope this helps
>
> Henrik
>

> > You have to rename the CEL files by replacing 'all _' (underscores)
> > with ',' (commas) to have filenames like CRL-2325D,Nsp.CEL and
> > CRL-2325D,Sty.CEL.  The *name* of a CEL file is defined in
> > aroma.affymetrix as the part of the filename before the first comma
> > (if any), i.e. with commas both CEL files have name 'CRL-2325D'.  All
> > other parts (except the filename extension) are referred to as *tags*,
> > i.e. the two CEL files have tags 'Nsp' and 'Sty', respectively.   If
> > you don't replace the underscores with commas, the name pf the two
> > files are 'CRL-2325D_Nsp' and 'CRL-2325D_Sty' and aroma.affymetrix
> > will not recognize them as being paired.  For more information on this
> > filename/directory name "grammar", please see Page 'Names, tags, and
> > filenames' at:
> >
> > http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/file--pathnames-2
> >
> > In other words, there is most likely no bug.  I have updated the
> > Vignette 'Paired total copy number analysis' explaining this.

> > under rawData/.  Just rename the corresponding CEL files under
> > probeData/ and plmData/ as well.  Most likely you should delete the

> > >      ...
> > >    Mapping250K_Sty/
> > >      CRL-2325D_Sty.CEL
> > >      ...
> > >
> > > You have to rename the CEL files by replacing 'all _' (underscores)
> > > with ',' (commas) to have filenames like CRL-2325D,Nsp.CEL and
> > > CRL-2325D,Sty.CEL.  The *name* of a CEL file is defined in
> > > aroma.affymetrix as the part of the filename before the first comma
> > > (if any), i.e. with commas both CEL files have name 'CRL-2325D'.  All
> > > other parts (except the filename extension) are referred to as *tags*,
> > > i.e. the two CEL files have tags 'Nsp' and 'Sty', respectively.   If
> > > you don't replace the underscores with commas, the name pf the two
> > > files are 'CRL-2325D_Nsp' and 'CRL-2325D_Sty' and aroma.affymetrix
> > > will not recognize them as being paired.  For more information on this
> > > filename/directory name "grammar", please see Page 'Names, tags, and
> > > filenames' at:
> > >
> > > http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/file--pathnames-2
> > >
> > > In other words, there is most likely no bug.  I have updated the
> > > Vignette 'Paired total copy number analysis' explaining this.
> > >
> > > You do not have to reran the analysis if you rename the CEL files
> > > under rawData/.  Just rename the corresponding CEL files under
> > > probeData/ and plmData/ as well.  Most likely you should delete the
> > > files under the cbsData/Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal/ directory.

> > > Hope this helps

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] How to extract copy-numbers from glad model
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] How to extract copy-numbers from glad model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Christian.

On Tue, Feb 26, 2008 at 12:44 AM,
<Christian...@vie.boehringer-ingelheim.com> wrote:
>
>
>
> Dear Henrik,
>
> Using aroma.affymetrix I have fitted a GLAD model and would like to extract
> the (relative) copy-numbers.
>
> Following the aroma-affymetrix website I did:
> # get cdf
> > chiptypes <- c("Mapping250K_Sty", "Mapping250K_Nsp")
> > cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chiptypes[1])
>
> # get cel
> > name <- "TestSty250K"
> > cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chiptypes[1])
>
> # correct for allelic cross talk
> > acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs)
> > csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)
>
> # quantile normalization
> > cs.ac <http://cs.ac> <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, tags="ACC,-XY",
> > chipType=chiptypes[1]) ac.qn  <- QuantileNormalization(cs.ac <http://cs.ac>) csCN <-
> > process(ac.qn, verbose=verbose)
>
> # normalization for sequence effects
> > cesNList <- list()
> > fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces) cesNList[[chiptypes[1]]] <-
> > process(fln, verbose=verbose) cesN <- cesNList[[chiptypes[1]]]
>
> # fit GLAD model
> > glad <- GladModel(cesNList)
> > ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(glad)
> > process(ce, verbose=verbose)
>
> Since ChromosomeExplorer can use the copy numbers for display, my question
> is: How can now I extract the raw copy-numbers and the fitted copy-numbers
> from the fitted GLAD model "glad"?

For any CopyNumberSegmentationModel (e.g. GladModel and CbsModel), the
method getRegions() returns the identified CN regions.  If the
segmentation still not have been done for the requested
array/chromosome it will be done (fit() is called internally).
Example:

cnrs <- getRegions(glad, arrays=1, chromosomes=1:4)
str(cnrs)
List of 1
 $ 0001-7:'data.frame': 4 obs. of  6 variables:
  ..$ chromosome: int [1:4] 1 2 3 4
  ..$ start     : num [1:4] 3122295  157739  653347  398952
  ..$ stop      : num [1:4] 2.45e+08 2.41e+08 1.99e+08 1.91e+08
  ..$ mean      : num [1:4] -0.0046 -0.0051 -0.0161 -0.008
  ..$ count     : num [1:4] 769 835 703 696
  ..$ url       : Factor w/ 4 levels "http://genome.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgTracks?cl
ade=vertebrate&org=Human&db=hg17&position=chr1%3A0-NA",..: 1 2 3 4

The 'url' field/column is add for convenience, but unfortunately it is
rather hardwired.  To change organism or genome version, you have to
change arguments:

cnrs <- getRegions(glad, arrays=1, chromosomes=1:4, organism =
"Human", hgVersion="hg18")

I also realized while writing this that the output of 'url' is broken
(all regions are [0,NA]).  That will be fixed in the next release.

>
> This is what I tried w/o success:
> > tmp <- getRawCnData(glad, cesNList)
> # Exception: Argument 'ceList' contains a non-ChipEffectFile:
> CnChipEffectSet
>
> What kind of list do I need here?
> Is this the correct method to use?

That function was setup as an internal support method not (yet)
intended to be used "in public". [It takes two lists of
ChipEffect*File*:s, one for the nominator and one for the denominator,
so it can calculate the raw CNs for a *single* array (where the
elements in each list correspond to a chip type).  You tried to pass a
list of ChipEffect*Set*:s (containing all arrays not one).]

There is currently no method for retrieving the raw CN estimates from
the segmentation model class.    Note that the GLAD or CBS method does
not calculate their own raw CNs, but use the ones we estimate in the
steps before the segmentation.

Instead, as you point out below (Vignette 'Calculating raw total copy
numbers manually' I guess), the best you can do now is to use theta <-
extractMatrix(ces) [next release also extractDataFrame()] to retrieve
the chip effect estimates and then calculate the raw CNs from there.
I realize that that is less convenient because you i) have to manually
get the genomic positions and sort the data yourself, but also ii) if
you use two chip types (e.g. 100K or 500K) you have to merge the
estimates yourself.  This approach also requires you to load estimates
across all arrays in order to calculate the robust average.

I'll see if I have time to implement a more convenient extractRawCNs()
method for segmentation model.

>
> Then I tried to extract the data from the files in directory "gladData":
> > tmp <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name,
> > tags="QN,ACC,-XY,RMA,A+B,FLN,-XY", chipType=chiptypes[1],
> paths=c("gladData"))
> # Exception: No files found:
> gladData/TestSty250K,QN,ACC,-XY,RMA,A+B,FLN,-XY/Mapping250K_Sty
>
> Interestingly, the files in
> "gladData/TestSty250K,QN,ACC,-XY,RMA,A+B,FLN,-XY/Mapping250K_Sty" do exist!
> What is the reason for this?

No this is not right.  The gladData/ directory contains files holding
the GLAD estimates.  These are not stored as CEL files and are hence
not CEL sets.  The error message is right reporting that it did not
find any (matching) files, because it could not find any CEL files
(which you asked for).

Currently the GLAD estimates are stored as binary R files saved with
saveObject() of R.utils and should be considered an internal file
format that might be changed in the future (if there ever will be a
standard file format for segmentation estimates).

>

Cheers

Henrik

> P.S.: I can extract the raw copy-numbers manually as described on the
> web-site, but not the fitted (and raw) copy-numbers from glad.
>
> Thank you in advance
> Best regards
> Christian
>
>
>
>
>
>
>
>
>
>  >
>

messages.subject: Newbie Question -- How to choose Reference for CNAG Non-paired Test, Affy 500K chip
messages.subject_clean: Newbie Question -- How to choose Reference for CNAG Non-paired Test, Affy 500K chip
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I'm a newbie of this forum; also I'm very new to microarray analysis.
I would like to do some learning on using CNV on Autism data.  I have
allocated (a) a dataset on GEO that used Affy 500K SNPs chip for
genotyping of trios (probands and some parents).  (b) CNAG 2.0.   I
would like to apply CNAG2.0 on the data downloaded from GEO, using non-
paired TEST and REFERENCE.

Would the experts tell me:
a.  What is Reference used in CNAG?
     a.1.  Should Reference be genotyped of non-autism (in this case)
individuals, and TEST is for genotyped data of affected (autism)
individuals?  Or vice versa?  Or it depends on what I would like to
study?
     a.2.  Does the Reference data need to be 500K as well?  can it be
10K?  I assume that 500K reference shoudld be preferable.
     a.3   Does anyone know where to get 500K Genotyped control data?

b.  How does aroma.affymetrix compare to dnaCopy in bioconductor?

Many thanks in advance for any help.

Yoshi C.

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Newbie Question -- How to choose Reference for CNAG Non-paired Test, Affy 500K chip
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Newbie Question -- How to choose Reference for CNAG Non-paired Test, Affy 500K chip
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yoshi,

On Thu, Feb 28, 2008 at 5:32 PM, Yoshi <Yoshi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>  Hi All,
>
>  I'm a newbie of this forum; also I'm very new to microarray analysis.
>  I would like to do some learning on using CNV on Autism data.  I have
>  allocated (a) a dataset on GEO that used Affy 500K SNPs chip for
>  genotyping of trios (probands and some parents).  (b) CNAG 2.0.   I
>  would like to apply CNAG2.0 on the data downloaded from GEO, using non-
>  paired TEST and REFERENCE.

So, first of all, aroma.affymetrix does not do implement the CNAG
model/method explicitly although you could "imitate" it with some
knowledge.

>
>  Would the experts tell me:
>  a.  What is Reference used in CNAG?

CNAG v2 is using the *selected subset* of the *pool of all test
samples* to calculate its reference.  Please see the Nannya et al.
(2005) for details.

>      a.1.  Should Reference be genotyped of non-autism (in this case)
>  individuals, and TEST is for genotyped data of affected (autism)
>  individuals?  Or vice versa?  Or it depends on what I would like to
>  study?

I'm not sure what you are asking here and especially what you mean by
"vice versa".

To do copy number analysis you do *not* have to genotype your arrays.
It has been suggested that this can improve the power, but most models
do not require genotype calls, including CNAT, CNAG, dChip, and CRMA
(Bengtsson et al 2008; see website).

>      a.2.  Does the Reference data need to be 500K as well?  can it be
>  10K?  I assume that 500K reference shoudld be preferable.

Yes.  Since the raw CNs are calculated as a ratio between test and
reference at every locus, you need a reference estimate at each locus
of your test sample.  For many different reasons, I do not see that it
is possible to extrapolate from a lower-density array, actually not
even from a higher-density array.

>      a.3   Does anyone know where to get 500K Genotyped control data?

HapMap data.

>
>  b.  How does aroma.affymetrix compare to dnaCopy in bioconductor?

aroma.affymetrix is an R framework to do various modeling of
Affymetrix data, e.g. several different normalization methods are
available as well as probe-summarization models.  For CN analysis,
aroma.affymetrix implements, via wrappers to existing, the GLAD
('GLAD' package) and CBS ('DNAcopy' package) segmentation methods.
So, given the same raw CN estimates, aroma.affymetrix gives identical
CN regions as if you would have called CBS of DNAcopy explicitly.

What we this far have achieved and what is implemented in
aroma.affymetrix is an preprocessing method called CRMA (Bengtsson et
al 2008) that provides improved raw CN estimates that hopefully allows
the segmentation methods downstream to perform better.

Hope this helps

/Henrik

>
>  Many thanks in advance for any help.
>
>  Yoshi C.
>  >
>

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.9.0 released
messages.subject_clean: aroma.affymetrix v0.9.0 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

after more than two months of no updates the next version of
aroma.affymetrix has finally arrived.  As previous versions will no
longer be supported, please update to aroma.affymetrix v0.9.0
according to the instructions on:

  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix

Several things have been updated and corrected and overall the package
have been made even more robust and does more validations internally.
Here are a few paragraphs summarization the major updates:

Now extractMatrix() can be called on single files and not only on file
sets, e.g. ChipEffectFile/ChipEffectSet and FirmaFile/FirmaSet will
work.  The extractDataFrame() method was added to complement
extractMatrix() by preceeding the data columns with columns 'unit',
'group', and 'cell' containing indices.  In addition, by using
argument 'addNames=TRUE' the first two columns are 'unitName' and
'groupName' inferred from the CDF.

Boxplot statistics for NUSE and RLE was broken for data sets where the
unit groups have been merged.  Thanks to a lot of help from Elizabeth
Purdom this has now been fixed.  The NUSE/RLE scores can now be
retrieved either as boxplot statistics or for each unit separately.
As everything else in the package, it is done in a memory efficient
way, e.g. the boxplot statistics are calculated array by array so
there is no limitation of the number arrays.  Given a ChipEffectSet,
you can get the unit-specific NUSE scores from extractMatrix(ces,
field="NUSE") and the boxplot statistics as boxplotStats(ces, "NUSE").
 To plot, use plotBoxplot(ces, "NUSE").  Note that these do not
require setting up a QualityAssessmentModel, although that is still
supported as well.

The RmaPlm class will now turn to the faster but less accurate median
polish algorithm for very large probesets (> 500 probes; can be
changed via settings).  Such large probesets are often not of interest
but will be extremely slow to fit with the default regression model
(as reported a few timess).

For very large data sets (> 500 arrays; can be changed via settings),
the default is now not to report the range of CEL header timestamps
when calling print(), other the reading of the timestamp for each CEL
file will add up and print() will be slow.  Furthermore, for large
data sets one can also speed up the AffymetrixCelSet$byName(...) by
adding argument 'force=FALSE' (default to TRUE for now), which then
means that it will find the outcome in the file cache the next time it
is called.  This avoid a lot of validation checks etc.  Also,
timestamps for some Calvin CEL files were previously reported as NA,
which has now been fixed.

It is now possible to hiding annotation data files from
aroma.affymetrix by placing them in a subdirectory prefixed with a
period/dot, e.g.
annotationData/chipType/GenomeWideSNP_6/.archive/SomeFile.ufl.  That
will allow you to keep old versions of annotation files around.

For all methods that operates specifically on SNP and/or CN units,
these unit classes are now identified using the internal 'unit type'
field in the CDF.  This is how it should be, but before they were
identified by the unit names.  This updates makes it possible to
process custom SNP chips.

Finally, as mention in a previous message a week ago, you have to
download new UGP and UFL files, if you are using those in your
analysis.  The new ones contain the same information as previous
version, but due to a change in the file format, the latter will give
an informative error message.

Here are the package history details:

Version: 0.9.0 [2008-02-29]
o UPDATE/ROBUSTNESS: Now AromaUnitTabularBinaryFile:s stores the
  chip type in the file footer.  This allows us to identify the
  correct file gives a full chip type.  Because of this update,
  old UFL and UGP files become incompatible with the class and new
  version have to be downloaded.  The chip type can be queried by
  getChipType().  It is now also asserted that the number of units
  in the file match the number of units in the corresponding CDF.
o TIME OPTIMIZATION: Now RmaPlm and ExonRmaPlm turn to median polish
  if there are more than 500 cells *and* 6 arrays in the unit group.
  Option: aroma.affymetrix.settings$models$RmaPlm$medianPolishThreshold.
  Moreover, if the unit group is ridiculously large (5000 cells), the
  unit group is skipped and all returned estimates are NAs.
  Option: aroma.affymetrix.settings$models$RmaPlm$skipThreshold.
o TIME OPTIMIZATION: Now as.character() for AffymetrixCelSet reports
  time stamps only for data set with less than 500 arrays.
  Option: aroma.affymetrix.settingsoutput$timestampsThreshold.
o UPDATE: Annotation data directories starting with a period are no
  longer searched when looking for annotation data files.
o UPDATE: GcContentNormalization would only normalize SNP units but
  now also CN probes are normalized.
o UPDATE: Now a CnPlm with combineAlleles=TRUE also handles SNPs
  with six groups; they occur at least once in a custom SNP CDF.
o GENERALIZED: Now SNPs and CN probes are infered from the CDF unit
  type and no longer from the unit names.
o Added boxplotStats() to ChipEffectSet for calculating NUSE or RLE
  boxplot statistics (also on a subset of arrays).
o Added getUnitTypes() for AffymetrixCdfFile.
o Added extractMatrix() and extractDataFrame() to Parameter{File|Set},
  i.e. subclasses ChipEffect{File|Set} and Firma{File|Set} got it too.
o Added published paper to citation("aroma.affymetrix").
o CLEANUP: Now byName() can be used everywhere fromName() can be used.
  Same for byChipType() and fromChipType().
o BUG FIX: The methods for calculating boxplot statistics did not
  handle "merged" CDF units correctly giving incorrect results.
o BUG FIX/ROBUSTNESS: It was possible to set a non-compatible
  CDF when using static fromFiles() of AffymetrixCelSet.
o MEMORY OPTIMIZATION: Now importFromDChip() for CnChipEffectSet uses
  much less memory when infering the cell indices.
o BUG FIX: getTimestamp() for AffymetrixCelFile would return NA for
  Calvin files.  Now they are also supported.
o BUG FIX: getCellIndices() of CnChipEffectFile would return an error
  if 'units==NULL'.
o Updated importFromDChip() for CnChipEffectSet so that it imports data
  exported by more recent versions of dChip.  In recent versions the
  standard-error columns are named '*SE' whereas before it were '*SD'.
  In either case, standard errors were exported (confirmed by author).
MAINLY FOR DEVELOPERS:
o CLEANUP: Renamed getMonoCell() to getMonocellCdf() and
  createMonoCell() to createMonocellCdf(), because the former had
  strange names.
o CLEANUP: Renamed usage of getCellMap() to getUnitGroupCellMap().
  For backward compatibility, the old ones remain for a while.
o BUG FIX: Since 'affy' defines standardGeneric("colnames") and
  S3 methods are not found by such S4 generic functions, we avoid
  that method name, and instead use getColumnNames().
o BETA: Added static importFromApt() for CnChipEffectSet.
o BETA: Added classes AffymetrixAptSummaryFile and AffymetrixCnChpFile.
o BETA: Added class AromaUfcFile.
o BETA: Added classes DChipChpFile and DChipChpSet.
o BETA: Added class AlleleSummation.

Enjoy!

Henrik
